source.title: Unleashing Mask: Explore the Intrinsic Out-of-Distribution Detection Capability
source.authors: Jia-Ning Zhu; Hengzhuang Li; Jiang-Chao Yao; Tong-Liang Liu; Jianliang Xu; Bo Han

page_placements.theme: OOD detection and downstream metrics can decouple from in-distribution error

record.file_problem: none; full paper and appendices are present
record.tranche_reason: The study discusses training dynamics and conventional overfitting, but measures OOD-detection performance rather than the test-error curves or axes named by the claim versions. It neither tests nor relies on double descent as described in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports intermediate training stages with better OOD-detection performance than the final stage. These are results about OOD detection, not test error, and therefore do not test any listed version. The training-epoch OOD curves are shown as figures; exact curve values are not stated. Results cited from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study is about OOD detection. It measures OOD metrics (FPR95, AUROC, AUPR) across training epochs and proposes UM/UMAP. It does not sweep model size, sample size or label noise, and does not examine test-error curves for a second descent. Belkin et al. (2019), an original source, is cited only to define conventional overfitting (Appendix D). Figure 2(a) shows ID test loss and accuracy over 100 epochs, reported as still improving, but this is one clean-label run used only to rule out overfitting. It is not a test of epoch-wise double descent.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors find an intermediate training stage with better OOD detection than the final stage. They attribute the later decline to memorizing atypical ID samples and state this is not conventional overfitting, since test loss is still decreasing. They propose UM/UMAP to recover this capability.
record.recipe_differences: The study investigates OOD-detection dynamics and proposes Unleashing Mask; it does not reproduce the original double-descent methods or measure the claim's test-error curves.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported OOD-detection dynamics are examined across OOD datasets, learning-rate schedules, model structures, and ID datasets; the paper reports that the intermediate-stage observation occurs across these settings.

fits_no_version.finding: OOD-detection performance (FPR95, AUROC, AUPR) is better at an intermediate training checkpoint than at the final one. This holds across learning-rate schedules, DenseNet-101 and WRN-40-4, and CIFAR-10/100, while ID test accuracy keeps improving.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In image classifiers trained on ID data, OOD-detection performance peaks at an intermediate epoch even as ID test performance continues to improve; the authors attribute this to memorizing atypical samples.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 202 (2023)
record.problems: The study does not measure the test error, model-size sweep, sample-size sweep, or effective complexity specified by the claim. The training-trajectory values are presented in figures without exact text-readable values; the paper reports multiple-run results but does not state uncertainty for these plotted curves.
record.rows_left_out: No other claim-relevant results were omitted. Detailed OOD-detection comparisons of UM/UMAP against other methods are not rows because they do not measure any listed claim version; cited results from other studies are also excluded.

untested.parts: All: no model-size sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
All: the epoch curves are OOD metrics; the ID test loss in Fig. 2(a) comes from a single clean-label run and is not analysed for double descent.
All: no sample-size sweep near interpolation.
All: no capacity sweeps across model classes.
All: no label-noise manipulation. Weight decay and dropout are compared only on OOD metrics (Tables 6–9), not on a test-error peak.

record.verdict_notes: Relation changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only': double descent itself is never discussed; Belkin et al. is cited once in the overfitting definition. All rows correctly carry versions ['none'] and the state cannot_determine with respect to the claim.

versions.untested_parts: Model-size sweep and test error near the interpolation threshold.
Test error over epochs; the reported epoch curves measure OOD-detection performance instead.
Changing training sample size near an interpolation threshold and measuring test error.
Capacity sweeps and risk across model classes.
A unified effective-complexity measure predicting peak locations.
Noise, regularization, and multiple-peak behavior of test risk.
Recounting complexity by effective parameter number and testing the resulting risk curve.
